title: Set 103

sentences.ko: 올해부터 애들 태우는 줄이 건물 반대편으로 옮겨졌어. 그래서 이제 차에서 5분이 아니라 20분을 기다려. 조금만 늦어도 애가 건물 앞에 혼자 서 있고. 너희 애도 3시에 끝나? 아니면 어린 애들만 3시야? 솔직히 너도 어차피 그쪽으로 가는 거면 운전 번갈아 하고 싶은데.
sentences.text: They moved the pickup line to the other side of the building this year, so now I'm sitting in the car for twenty minutes instead of five, and if I'm running even a little late he's standing out front by himself. Does yours get out at three, or is it just the little ones? Because honestly I'd split the driving with you if you're going that way anyway.

alts.text: Pickup's on the other side of the building now, so I'm stuck in the car twenty minutes instead of five, and if I'm even a little late he's out front on his own. Is yours out at three too, or is that just the little kids? Cause honestly I'd split the driving with you if you're headed that way anyway.

The pickup line was relocated to the other side of the building this year, so I now wait in the car for twenty minutes rather than five, and if I am running even slightly late, he is left standing out front by himself. Does yours finish at three, or is that only the younger children? I would gladly share the driving with you if you are going that way regardless.

sentences.note: **pickup line** 은 학교 앞에서 차로 아이를 태워 가려고 줄 서는 자리를 말합니다. 학교가 끝나 아이가 나오는 것은 **get out at three** 처럼 get out 을 씁니다. **split the driving** 은 운전을 나눠서 번갈아 하는 것입니다.

sentences.ko: 은행 옆에 새로 생긴 데를 가 봤는데 빈자리가 하나도 없더라. 그래서 역 옆에 있는 데까지 걸어갔는데 거기도 똑같았어. 다들 노트북에 에코백 하나씩 놓고 앉아 있고. 커피는 처음 간 데서 이미 계산해 버려서 컵만 들고 길에 서 있었지. 결국 추운데 벤치에 앉아서 마셨어. 이러려던 게 아니었는데.
sentences.text: I tried that new place by the bank and there wasn't one open table, so I walked down to the one by the station and it was the same thing, everybody with a laptop and a tote bag. And I'd already paid for the coffee at the first place, so I'm standing out on the sidewalk holding it. I ended up drinking it on a bench in the cold, which is not what I had in mind.

alts.text: So I hit that new spot by the bank and there wasn't one free table, so I walked down to the one by the station and same deal, everyone with a laptop and a tote bag. And I'd already paid for my coffee at the first place, so there I am out on the sidewalk holding it. Ended up drinking it on a bench in the cold, which is not what I was going for.

I tried the new place near the bank and there was not a single open table, so I walked down to the one by the station and found the same situation, everyone with a laptop and a tote bag. I had already paid for the coffee at the first place, so I was left standing on the sidewalk holding it. I ended up drinking it on a bench in the cold, which was not what I had in mind.

sentences.note: **it was the same thing** 은 가는 곳마다 똑같은 상황이었다는 말입니다. 기대와 다르게 끝났을 때 **not what I had in mind** 라고 합니다.

sentences.ko: 잠드는 건 잘 자. 그게 답답한 점이야. 그런데 두 시간쯤 지나면 눈이 완전히 떠져서, 그때부터 밖이 밝아질 때까지 깨어 있어. 다들 그러라고 하니까 점심 뒤로는 커피를 끊었는데, 아무것도 안 달라졌어. 이제 오후 커피도 못 마시고 잠도 여전히 못 자.
sentences.text: I fall asleep fine, that's the part that gets me. But about two hours later I'm wide awake, and then I'm up until it starts getting light outside. I cut out coffee after lunch because that's what everybody tells you to do, and it didn't change anything. So now I don't get my afternoon coffee and I still don't sleep.

alts.text: Falling asleep is fine, that's the part that gets me. But two hours later I'm wide awake, and then I'm up till it starts getting light out. I cut out coffee after lunch cause that's what everybody tells you to do, and nothing changed. So now I don't get my afternoon coffee and I still don't sleep.

I fall asleep without difficulty, which is the part I find troubling. About two hours later, however, I am completely awake, and I remain awake until it begins to grow light outside. I gave up coffee after lunch because that is what everyone advises, and it changed nothing. So now I go without my afternoon coffee and I still do not sleep.

sentences.note: **wide awake** 는 잠이 완전히 깨서 정신이 또렷한 상태입니다. **cut out coffee** 는 커피를 아예 끊는 것이고, **that's the part that gets me** 는 바로 그 점이 답답하다는 말입니다.

sentences.ko: 코트도 못 벗었는데 이모가 애 언제 하나 더 낳느냐고 묻더라. 그러고는 저녁 먹을 때 삼촌이 다들 있는 앞에서 또 그 얘기를 꺼냈어. 나쁜 뜻으로 하는 말이 아닌 걸 아는데, 그래서 아무 말도 못 하는 거야. 그래서 저녁 내내 부엌에서 아무도 닦아 달라고 안 한 그릇을 닦고 있었어.
sentences.text: My aunt asked me when we're having another baby before I even got my coat off, and then my uncle started it up again at dinner in front of everybody. And I know they don't mean anything by it, which is exactly why I can't say anything back. So I spent most of the night in the kitchen drying dishes nobody asked me to dry.

alts.text: I hadn't even got my coat off and my aunt's asking when we're having another baby, and then my uncle starts it up again at dinner in front of everyone. And I know they don't mean anything by it, which is exactly why I can't say anything back. So I spent most of the night in the kitchen drying dishes nobody asked me to dry.

My aunt asked when we are having another baby before I had even taken my coat off, and then my uncle raised it again at dinner in front of everyone. I know they mean nothing by it, which is precisely why I cannot say anything in return. So I spent most of the night in the kitchen drying dishes that no one had asked me to dry.

sentences.note: **they don't mean anything by it** 은 상대가 나쁜 뜻 없이 한 말이라는 뜻입니다. **started it up again** 은 끝난 얘기를 또 꺼냈다는 말입니다.
sentences.situation: 친척들 모인 자리에서 질문 공세 받은 얘기

sentences.ko: 건강검진 받으러 갔는데 다 괜찮게 나왔어. 혈압만 높게 나왔는데, 의사가 병원에 왔다는 것만으로 혈압이 오르는 사람이 많다고 하더라. 그래서 지금 집에 그 작은 혈압계를 하나 두고 2주 동안 하루에 두 번 숫자를 적어야 해. 그러고 있으면 오히려 혈압이 올라갈 것 같은데.
sentences.text: I went in for my physical and everything came back fine, except my blood pressure was up, and she said that happens to a lot of people just from being at the doctor. So now I've got one of those little cuffs at home and I'm supposed to write down the number twice a day for two weeks. Which is the kind of thing that's going to make it go up.

alts.text: Had my physical and everything came back fine, except my blood pressure was up, and she said that happens to tons of people just from being at the doctor. So now there's one of those little cuffs sitting at home and I'm supposed to write the number down twice a day for two weeks. Which is exactly the kind of thing that's gonna make it go up.

I went in for my physical and all of the results were fine, except that my blood pressure was elevated, and she said that happens to a great many people simply from being at the doctor. So I now have one of those small cuffs at home and I am meant to record the number twice a day for two weeks. Which is the sort of thing that is going to make it rise.

sentences.note: 검사 결과가 괜찮게 나왔다고 할 때 **came back fine** 이라고 합니다. **my blood pressure was up** 처럼 수치가 높게 나온 것을 up 하나로 말합니다. **the kind of thing that's going to make it go up** 은 오히려 그걸 더 심하게 만들 일이라는 뜻입니다.
sentences.situation: 병원 갔다 온 얘기 가볍게 하기

reviewed: 5번 casual 이 text 와 첫 대목이 그대로 겹쳐서(Went in for my physical and everything came back fine) 말투를 바꾼 티가 안 났다. 시작을 Had my physical 로 바꾸고 뒤도 tons of / sitting at home / gonna 로 더 구어답게 고쳤다.
5번 한국어의 '혈압 띠' 는 한국에서 안 쓰는 말이라 '작은 혈압계' 로 고쳤다. 마지막 줄도 앞 문장을 그대로 되풀이하고 있어서 '그러고 있으면 오히려 혈압이 올라갈 것 같은데' 로 줄였다.
2번 한국어의 '천가방' 을 실제로 쓰는 말인 '에코백' 으로 바꿨다(tote bag).
1번 한국어 마지막 줄이 '그쪽으로 다니면' 이라 누가 다니는 건지 흐렸다. 영어의 if you're going that way anyway 에 맞춰 '너도 어차피 그쪽으로 가는 거면' 으로 고쳤다. 첫 줄의 '태우러 가는 줄이 옮겨졌어' 도 번역투라 다듬었다.
